articles.title: Ainsley Earhardt and Sean Hannity marry at the same church where they got engaged
articles.summary: Fox News stars Ainsley Earhardt and Sean Hannity tied the knot on Saturday at the historic Church of Bethesda-by-the-Sea in Palm Beach, Florida.
articles.body: Fox News stars Ainsley Earhardt and Sean Hannity tied the knot on Saturday at the historic Church of Bethesda-by-the-Sea in Palm Beach, Florida, returning to the place where Hannity proposed over Christmas in 2024. Surrounded by their children, relatives and closest friends, the couple exchanged vows in a heartfelt ceremony that reflected their shared faith and the importance of family in their lives. The setting brought their engagement story full circle, as they were married at the same church where they first committed to spending their lives together. Earhardt and Hannity incorporated their shared faith into the ceremony with selected readings from Romans 12 and the Song of Solomon. Romans 12 emphasizes devotion and respect, encouraging believers to "Love one another with brotherly affection" and "Outdo one another in showing honor" (Romans 12:10), while the Song of Solomon speaks to the strength of romantic love, stating, "Many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it" (Song of Solomon 8:7). The selections reflected the values the couple hopes to carry into their marriage. During the ceremony, which was officiated by the couple's ministers, Earhardt and Hannity exchanged personal vows, reflecting on their love for each other, their shared faith and the life they look forward to building together. The bride wore a gown by Oscar de la Renta for the occasion. Following the ceremony, guests gathered under a retractable roof for a private reception under the stars at the Everglades Club in Palm Beach, where the newlyweds celebrated alongside loved ones from different chapters of their lives. The wedding brought together relatives and longtime friends, including those who have known Hannity since his early days on Long Island and Earhardt's close friends from South Carolina, as well as colleagues who have been part of their careers over the years. Among the guests were FOX News Media CEO Suzanne Scott, Fox News president and executive editor Jay Wallace and anchors and hosts, including: Steve Doocy, Lawrence Jones, Brian Kilmeade, Laura Ingraham, Mark Levin, Dana Perino, Bret Baier, Harris Faulkner, Emily Compagno, Bill Hemmer, Martha MacCallum, Kayleigh McEnany, Carley Shimkus, and Trey Gowdy among others. Fox News host Lara Trump and Eric Trump also attended and were joined by newly minted Fox News contributor Karoline Leavitt and White House chief of staff Susie Wiles. Among the other guests in attendance were casino mogul Steve Wynn, philanthropist Julia Koch, entrepreneur and podcast host Patrick Bet-David, podcast host Sage Steele, country music star Lee Greenwood, fitness and podcast personality Jillian Michaels, television personality Nancy Grace, Rascal Flatts frontman Gary LeVox and Five for Fighting's John Ondrasik. Also celebrating the couple at the wedding were Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis and his wife Casey, White House Deputy Chief of Staff Dan Scavino and his wife Erin, Sen. Tim Scott and his wife Molly, U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz, former House Speaker Newt Gingrich and his wife, former Ambassador Callista Gingrich. For Earhardt and Hannity, the wedding was a celebration of more than their marriage. It was a reflection of the faith, friendship and love that brought them together, made especially meaningful by exchanging vows in the same church where their journey toward marriage began. In joint remarks made following the wedding celebration, the newly married couple said, "Our hearts are overflowing with love and gratitude as we begin this new chapter together as husband and wife. To exchange our vows in our home church where we got engaged, surrounded by our children, families and dearest friends, was more meaningful than we could have ever imagined. Our faith has always been at the center of our relationship, and we truly believe God brought us together. We feel blessed by the outpouring of love and support from the wonderful people in our lives and are excited for the future. Above all, we are grateful to God for bringing us to this moment and for the beautiful life we will continue to build together." Prior to Saturday’s wedding, Earhardt and Hannity hosted a private pre-wedding celebration Friday night at Mar-a-Lago in Palm Beach, where President Donald Trump and first lady Melania Trump joined the couple's family and friends. The president did not attend Saturday's wedding ceremony.

articles.title: Bulgarians vote for president in shadow of Russia’s war in Ukraine
articles.summary: The two leading candidates condemn recent deadly Black Sea drone strikes, but differ on the Ukraine war more broadly.
articles.body:
Bulgarians are voting in a presidential election amid the spread of Russia’s war on Ukraine to the waters off Bulgaria’s Black Sea coast.

Ahead of Sunday’s vote, President Iliana Iotova, 61, and ex-caretaker Prime ⁠Minister Andrey Gyurov, 50, were leading a field of 27 candidates in the polls.

⁠The presidency is a largely ceremonial post in Bulgaria. While major policies must be approved by Parliament, direct election gives the president greater political authority. The president leads the armed forces and can veto legislation, sign international treaties and appoint ambassadors.

The election has also gained attention after a series of drone attacks on merchant ships off Bulgaria’s coast that likely killed some two dozen international seafarers.

The drone strikes ‌sparked international condemnation and concerns about the growing reach of the war in Ukraine, prompting Bulgaria to seek allied assistance to bolster its maritime security.

The Bulgarian government has stopped short of explicitly blaming Russia for the attacks, but Prime Minister Rumen Radev said the outcome of the strikes “benefits the Russian Federation”.

The two leading candidates for president have both condemned the strikes, but they differ on the broader war in Ukraine.

Gyurov, who served as caretaker prime minister this year, is backed by ⁠pro-Western, reformist parties and has long expressed support for Ukraine. He ⁠signed a security cooperation agreement with Kyiv during his time as premier.

“I want Bulgaria to have a voice of its own in Europe, a reliable NATO ally that defends its interests through preparedness, strong diplomacy and ⁠a clear position,” he said at a rally on Thursday.

Iotova, a former vice president, became acting president in January after Radev resigned to ⁠enter the parliamentary race, which he won on what many ⁠political analysts considered a Kremlin-friendly ticket.

Radev supports Iotova, and they both call for a diplomatic end to the war.

“My opponents argue that there must be ‌a war of attrition,” Iotova told a rally on Thursday. “The truth is, we are all the ones who are most exhausted.”

While there is a broad consensus among the parties in Parliament on the country’s pro-Western path, widespread pro-Russian sentiments based on traditional historical and cultural ties with Russia have divided society, particularly since the start of Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Dobromir Zhivkov, managing director of the Market Links polling agency, said Iotova is among those who advocate that Bulgaria take a more neutral position.

“They call for an end to aid for Ukraine and a halt to arms deliveries to Ukraine; we often hear them use Kremlin rhetoric and terminology borrowed directly from Kremlin propaganda,” he told The Associated Press news agency earlier this week.

Candidates are also addressing public fears about the steep rise in energy prices and surging inflation, with many Bulgarians in rural areas struggling to make ends meet.

Polls by Alpha Research give Iotova 41 percent of the vote and ‌Gyurov ‌28 percent.

Voting starts at 7am (05:00 GMT), and polls close at 8pm (18:00 GMT).

Analysts expect none of the 27 candidates to secure the outright majority needed to win in the first round, however.

Turnout must also be above 50 percent of the 6.6 million registered voters, and Sunday’s turnout is expected to be less than 40 percent, which means a likely run-off on November 1.

articles.title: Budget to include £1bn for social and affordable housing
articles.summary: The move will take funding for the 10-year programme to more than £40bn.
articles.body:
More than £1bn for social and affordable housing in England will be provided in the Budget, taking funding for the government's 10-year homes programme past £40bn.

Mayors and regional leaders across England are also expected to get greater powers and funding in Wednesday's announcement - with councils helped to borrow money from the government to invest in housebuilding through preferential interest rates.

It is hoped the plans will give regional leaders more flexibility and authority over investment decisions.

Chancellor John Healey said English cities and regions would get the "right to decide their own future", while Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the plans were about shifting power to those "who know their communities best".

The chancellor will also announce more support for small breweries with the Treasury saying he wants "to turn the tide for our pint producers".

Meanwhile, the Sunday Times reports that Healey is expected to unveil billions of pounds of new defence spending in the Budget. Specific details on the funding would be outlined at next year's spending review

But shadow chancellor Andrew Griffith has called for Healey to resign if he fails to set out how the UK will spend 3% of the UK's GDP on defence by 2030.

What is the Budget and what could be in it?

Between quick wins and big dreams lies Burnham's biggest test

Under the plans for the regions, an initial £285m in transitional seed funding will be allocated by the government next year to support mayors and local leaders - and reduce reliance on "fragmented bidding pots" in Whitehall, the Treasury said.

The government will also confirm that it will work with mayors to design a new £1.5bn borrowing facility from 2028, which would allow them to access capital needed to support local priorities.

The Treasury said this could be put towards new homes, bringing high streets back to life, or improving transport links.

Healey said: "Mayors and local leaders know what their communities need to grow, which is why we are giving them more money, more power and more capacity to get projects moving, build homes and make the right decisions for their areas."

Areas across the country which are not yet strategic authorities will be able to access a share of the £285m funding to "unlock projects which will contribute to growth in their areas".

The prime minister said: "I'm calling time on local leaders going cap in hand to Westminster. That is no way to run a country."

Claire Ward, chairwoman of the UK Mayors Network and Labour's East Midlands mayor, said that having the "right powers and resources through increased devolution" would help turn "ambitious plans into reality and deliver real, lasting change" for communities.

Lord Sadiq Khan, Labour's mayor of London, said greater ability to invest could "help unlock transformational infrastructure projects" including the West London Orbital route, the extension of the Bakerloo Underground line and Docklands Light Railway, and the development of Stratford International station.

However, Healey's Budget preparations suffered a blow when the Treasury's entrepreneurship adviser, Alex Depledge, announced she was resigning from the role. She will leave on Thursday, the day after the Budget.

Start-ups, she told the Sunday Times , were being treated as a "sideshow" and should not be pushed to the "margins of economic policy".

"Keeping scale-ups on the fringes underestimates the contribution of our greatest companies, and we need to support and develop them on British shores at all costs," she said.

Leading up to the Budget, defence has also remained a key talking point. Healey resigned in June from his role as defence secretary in the previous government over the defence investment plan , which he claimed fell "well short" of what was needed to fund the armed forces.

He had called for defence spending to rise to 3% of the country's GDP by 2030, on the way to reaching a Nato target of 3.5% in 2035.

But urging him to commit to setting out plans to spend 3% of GDP on defence, the shadow chancellor said: "We are living in an era of extraordinary threats, and yet the chancellor is dithering over finding the money to pay the country's insurance premium... you cannot have a strong economy without a strong defence".

Responding to Andrew Griffith's comments, Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said the Conservatives were to blame for failing to invest in the military while in office.

Streeting said the prime minister had made it clear that his government was "determined to give our armed forces the investment needed to keep us safe".

articles.title: 49ers may have fewer than 48 players available against Falcons amid injury wave, coach Kyle Shanahan says
articles.summary: Christian Kirk is set to return from injured reserve as the 49ers rule out Mike Evans, Nick Bosa and Deebo Samuel ahead of the Falcons game.
articles.body: Every NFL team deals with injuries. It's an unfortunate part of the game. But few have been more defined by them in recent seasons than the San Francisco 49ers, whose injury report has seemed to become a weekly storyline. The undefeated 49ers made a cross-country trip this week for a matchup with the Atlanta Falcons. San Francisco will again be without several key players Sunday, including receiver Mike Evans, who is dealing with a sore Achilles, and defensive end Nick Bosa, who has a calf injury. The team’s receiver corps was already thin, with Ricky Pearsall, Deebo Samuel Sr., De’Zhaun Stribling and Demarcus Robinson unable to go Sunday. The 49ers also ruled out safety Marques Sigle and linebackers Garret Wallow and Luke Gifford for Week 7. Niners head coach Kyle Shanahan acknowledged the lengthy list of unavailable players and said the 49ers may not be able to reach the maximum 48 players on the game-day roster. 49ERS STAR WIDE RECEIVER RICKY PEARSALL OUT FOR THE SEASON, TO UNDERGO SURGERY ON KNEE IN CRUSHING BLOW Teams can elevate players from the practice squad when injuries leave them thin at a position, but Shanahan does not expect those moves to get San Francisco to 48 players Sunday. Instead, the former Falcons offensive coordinator said the 49ers have discussed preparing some players to line up outside their usual positions because of the injuries. Shanahan said the situation was a first in his coaching career. "I don't think ever in my career [has that happened]," he said. "It's a unique situation." Veteran receiver Christian Kirk is in line to make his season debut Sunday, Shanahan confirmed. His return from injured reserve would provide a welcome boost for the 49ers. Bosa recently shared an optimistic view about being able to return for Week 5 or 6, but the 49ers kept him out of practice to give him extra recovery time. That optimism seems caught Shanahan off guard, given how carefully Bosa usually assesses his own status. "I just think he was a little too optimistic, especially for Bosa because he's pretty accurate," Shanahan said. 49ERS GM QUELLS BUZZ AROUND ELECTRICAL SUBSTATION THEORY "He doesn't say stuff like that unless it's accurate. I just think it surprised him. He worked out after he said that to you guys and the next day was just a little sore, which surprised all of us, and that wasn't a great sign, especially going to playing turf and stuff this week." articles.title: Suspect in St. Louis teen’s fatal freeway shooting investigated in another roadway attack
articles.summary: The suspect in the fatal freeway shooting of a high school girl just outside St. Louis is being investigated in connection with a second roadway shooting, court documents show.
articles.body: The suspect in the fatal freeway shooting of a high school girl just outside St. Louis is being investigated in connection with a second roadway shooting, federal court documents show. Willie Herndon, a 42-year-old from Arlington, Texas, is accused of killing 17-year-old Alyssa Wilson on Oct. 14. In a federal complaint, investigators say a spent shell casing matching the one used in Alyssa’s shooting was found close to where a vehicle was struck on another freeway three days earlier. No one was reported injured in the Oct. 11 shooting in St. Louis proper. The federal complaint, filed in U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Illinois, states that a vehicle that had just exited Interstate 55 was hit by gunfire, and that security video showed a white SUV parked on the side of the interstate at the time before it “fled the scene immediately after the shooting.” “A single cartridge case was recovered,” the federal complaint states. “The cartridge case’s headstamp was the same manufacturer as the one recovered by investigators during Wilson’s murder investigation.” Lab testing is being conducted to determine if ballistic evidence ties the two crimes, according to the complaint. Herndon is scheduled to appear in U.S. District Court in East St. Louis on Tuesday for a hearing on his pretrial detention on a federal charge of being a felon with a gun, according to the documents, which state he was convicted of felonies in Los Angeles for taking a vehicle without consent in 2001 and for receiving known stolen property and burglary in 2015. Herndon is also scheduled to appear at a preliminary hearing on Nov. 4 in the same courthouse. His federal public defender did not respond to a request for comment. A high schooler’s life cut short Herndon was charged with first-degree murder and armed criminal action after his arrest in the killing of Alyssa, a high schooler from nearby Florissant, Missouri, who was driving to a St. Louis Zoo Halloween celebration when she was shot Oct. 14. “Alyssa was 17, excited about her life, excited about her future,” her father, Robert Hickman, said at a news conference Monday. “This was a senseless act.” Herndon’s wife, Taiya Herndon, allegedly drove the pair to an Illinois hotel roughly 12 miles from St. Louis after the attack, authorities said. She faces a state charge of hindering prosecution. Authorities have said Alyssa had no ties to the pair. It’s not clear if either defendant has been assigned counsel in the state cases. The public defender’s office for the St. Louis area did not respond to a request for comment. Following a search of the Herndons’ nearby Illinois hotel room after the attack, authorities said they found notebooks with handwritten entries, according to the federal criminal complaint. The entries included license plate numbers, descriptions of vehicles and descriptions of law enforcement personnel Willie Herndon believed were following him, the complaint said. On Oct. 2, the Herndons drove from Texas to Arkansas and then Missouri, arriving the next day, while using one of multiple Oklahoma license plates that did not belong to their white SUV, prosecutors alleged in the complaint. One plate was switched following Alyssa’s shooting, they said. Killing captured on security video Investigators relying on security video of the Oct. 14 attack said during Monday’s news conference someone in a white Buick Enclave stopped on the shoulder of the southbound side of Interstate 170 in Overland, Missouri, just outside St. Louis. That person got out, paced around and ultimately opened fire on Alyssa’s vehicle as it passed, authorities said. A single round penetrated the back of Alyssa’s vehicle and struck the teenager in the back, exiting through her chest, according to the federal complaint against Willie Herndon. She was 12 minutes into her journey to meet a friend at the zoo, it said. Alyssa was ultimately rushed to Barnes-Jewish Hospital in St. Louis, where she was pronounced dead, officials said. Using information from security video, including a license plate number for the white Buick and an Arkansas Razorbacks sticker on its liftgate, authorities tracked the SUV to a Days Inn in Caseyville, Illinois, where detectives spent hours staking it out on Oct. 15 and 16, authorities have said. When Taiya Herndon approached the vehicle, authorities rushed her, they said. When Willie Herndon soon emerged from the hotel afterward, authorities said, he ran and was also taken into custody. Matching shell casings The criminal complaint against Taiya Herndon stated that Willie Herndon admitted to investigators that he opened fire on the side of the freeway on Oct. 14, and that she admitted to driving. “When interviewed, Willie Herndon admitted to standing outside the passenger door of the vehicle on southbound Interstate 170, and discharging a rifle,” the state complaint states. “Taiya Hendon admitted to driving the white Buick Enclave.” A search of the Herndons’ hotel room turned up an American Built Custom Rifle Company version of the AR-15, a semiautomatic rifle, according to the federal criminal complaint. It was loaded with MaxxTech 23 7.62x39 ammunition, which matches the brand and size of spent shell casing investigators said they found at the side of Interstate 170 after the attack on Alyssa, according to the federal complaint. MaxxTech was also the maker of the spent casing found near the Oct. 11 attack, it said. Taiya Herndon is scheduled to appear for a hearing over the amount of her bail, set at $500,000 to be paid in full, on Thursday. Her preliminary hearing is scheduled for Nov. 19, according to state court records.

articles.title: 'Ignore strike calls': LPG distributor body ahead of Rahul Gandhi's rally in Delhi

articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Federation of LPG Distributors of India (FLDI) has opposed calls for protests and an indefinite strike in Delhi, urging distributors to continue supply and delivery operations ahead of the INDIA bloc's November 1 rally led by Rahul Gandhi at Ramlila Maidan.In a statement, the distributors' body said it was in talks with oil marketing companies (OMCs) and the petroleum ministry over distributors' demands and had received assurances of an early resolution.The FLDI said protests without exhausting avenues for dialogue were not a practical approach, stressing that uninterrupted LPG supply to consumers remained its priority."We urge all fellow distributors to continue with supply and delivery operations, ignoring unverified calls for action, so that no family faces any inconvenience," the federation said as quoted by news agency ANI.The development comes amid concerns over the impact of the INDIA bloc's rally on Delhi's commercial activity during the festive shopping season."The FLDI does not support the proposed protests and indefinite strike in Delhi. We advocate for meaningful dialogue, concrete decisions, and sustained efforts to address the legitimate demands of distributors. We are engaged in constructive dialogue with the Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) and the Ministry of Petroleum. The concerns of the distributors are being heard, and we have received assurances of an early resolution," it said."We believe that solutions can be achieved through dialogue and decisive action. Ensuring uninterrupted LPG service to consumers is our top priority. Dialogue with the OMCs and the Ministry is ongoing, and we have been assured of a resolution. Given this, resorting to protests without exhausting all avenues for dialogue is not a practical approach. Maintaining a regular and safe supply of LPG to consumers remains our primary objective," it added.On Saturday, the Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) urged Rahul Gandhi to postpone the November 1 rally, claiming it could disrupt business worth Rs 10,000 crore during the peak Diwali shopping period.CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal said traders had already suffered estimated losses of around Rs 3,000 crore in October due to rallies, marches and road closures in Connaught Place, India Gate and central Delhi.The INDIA bloc's rally is aimed at intensifying its campaign against alleged "vote chori" and demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: New York's archdiocese, survivors of clergy abuse agree to $800 million settlement
articles.summary: The Archdiocese of New York and attorneys for about 1,300 parishioners who said they were sexually abused by clergy have agreed to an $800 million settlement of their legal claims, the second-largest involving a Catholic archdiocese in the U.S.
articles.body: The Archdiocese of New York and attorneys for about 1,300 parishioners who said they were sexually abused by clergy have agreed to an $800 million settlement of their legal claims, the second-largest involving a Catholic archdiocese in the U.S. Archbishop Ronald Hicks sent an email Saturday to clergy confirming the settlement after attorneys for the survivors of alleged abuse announced it. Hicks said the agreement will not be final until the parties sign it, an action scheduled for the week of Nov. 6. The only larger settlement over sexual abuse claims in the U.S. was by the Archdiocese of Los Angeles, which agreed in 2024 to pay $880 million to 1,000 abuse victims, in addition to $740 million in claims it had paid previously. In June, the Archdiocese of San Francisco agreed to a $395 million settlement over about 500 lawsuits filed over clergy abuse, and in December 2025, a federal judge approved a settlement in which the Archdiocese of New Orleans agreed to pay at least $230 million to abuse victims. The agreement with the New York archdiocese would end more than seven years of lawsuits. The parties agreed to a framework for an agreement in May that required everyone who filed a claim to sign off. “The unanimous agreement of survivors who filed claims against the Archdiocese of New York marks a powerful moment in the pursuit of justice,” Jeff Anderson, an attorney representing people who filed more than 1,000 of claims against the Catholic Church in New York state, said in a statement. “Through their courage, sacrifice, and determination, survivors have helped bring about a reckoning and a meaningful step toward accountability.” The Archiocese of New York covers the city's boroughs of the Bronx, Manhattan and Staten Island, as well as seven counties to the north of New York City, and is home to about 300 churches, more than 150 parochial schools and 2.5 million Catholics. In his email to clergy, Hicks said that if church members ask about the settlement, “please let them know that much progress has been made.” “We are on the verge of being able to, please God, bring some measure of healing and reconciliation to all victim-survivors,” he wrote. “This agreement will also allow the archdiocese to turn its full attention once again to its mission of preaching the Gospel, healing the sick, caring for the poor and needy, welcoming the stranger, and educating our children.” A New York law enacted in 2019 allows survivors of child sexual abuse to file lawsuits against their abusers and institutions that shielded them until they turn 55. People who had already had turned 55 when the law was enacted also were given until August 2021 to file lawsuits, no matter when the alleged abuse occurred. “This is an extraordinary achievement for the survivors,” said Trusha Goffe, an attorney in Anderson’s firm. "The survivors remined resolute through years of litigation to reach this monumental settlement.”

articles.title: New York Archdiocese agrees to pay $800m to 1,300 sexual abuse survivors
articles.summary: The settlement is the second-largest after an $880m deal reached by the Archdiocese of Los Angeles in 2024.
articles.body:
The Archdiocese of New York has agreed to pay more than $800m to settle the legal claims of about 1,300 survivors of sexual abuse by clergy.

New York Archbishop Ronald Hicks said on Saturday that the settlement will be formally signed on November 6 after an agreement with the plaintiffs and their lawyers.

“We are on the verge of being able to, please God, bring some measure of healing and reconciliation to all victim-survivors,” he wrote in an email sent to his priests and shared by the archdiocese’s news outlet.

“This agreement will also allow the archdiocese to turn its full attention once again to its mission of preaching the Gospel, healing the sick, caring for the poor and needy, welcoming the stranger, and educating our children,” he added.

According to The New York Times, which broke the story, each of the approximately 1,300 survivors will receive at least $250,000 from the Archdiocese of New York and potentially more depending on the severity of the abuse suffered.

The settlement is the second-largest of its kind after an $880m deal reached by the Archdiocese of Los Angeles in 2024.

“The unanimous agreement of survivors who filed claims against the Archdiocese of New York marks a powerful moment in the pursuit of justice,” Jeff Anderson, a lawyer representing people who filed more than 1,000 claims against the Catholic Church in New York state, said in a statement.

“Through their courage, sacrifice, and determination, survivors have helped bring about a reckoning and a meaningful step toward accountability.”

The agreement marks the end of years of negotiations with lawyers representing the plaintiffs, as the Catholic Church in the United States has been mired in sexual abuse scandals since the early 2000s.

In the 2000s, media investigations revealed that Catholic priests in the US had committed sexual abuse against thousands of children over several decades, and that church leaders had often covered up these cases or transferred the offending priests instead of reporting them to civil authorities.

Dioceses across the country have had to pay hundreds of millions of dollars in damages, and programmes have been created to compensate survivors without going to trial.

In June, the Archdiocese of San Francisco announced it had reached an agreement to pay $395m to about 530 survivors of sexual abuse committed by its clergy to settle their lawsuits.

articles.title: Brazil’s election tests Lula’s leftist legacy against Bolsonaro’s right-wing movement
articles.summary: Brazilians return to the polls on Sunday to choose between two candidates campaigning on sharply different versions of the country amid growing concerns over crime, corruption, and a broader rightward shift among Latin American voters.
articles.body: Brazilians return to the polls on Sunday to choose between two candidates campaigning on sharply different versions of the country amid growing concerns over crime, corruption, and a broader rightward shift among Latin American voters. Leftist President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, 80, entered this month’s presidential election as the favorite by nearly every poll, hoping to secure a fourth term and extend a political career that has shaped the country for more than two decades. He instead has found himself in a runoff with Flávio Bolsonaro, the eldest son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, whose stronger-than-expected performance in a first round of voting upended predictions and turned one of Latin America’s most prominent left-wing leaders into the election’s underdog. The octogenarian’s challenge is to secure another term after a decades-long political career, while Bolsonaro, 45, attempts to keep his first-round momentum and carry it into a final victory. The outcome of Sunday’s vote will have repercussions far beyond Brazil. As right-wing governments gain ground across Latin America, the runoff could determine whether the region’s largest country becomes an ally of the Trump administration — if Flavio accomplishes something his father could not in 2022: defeat Lula at the ballot box. A first-round upset According to Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court, Bolsonaro secured 2.2 million votes more than Lula in the first round of voting. Neither candidate reached the majority needed to win outright, forcing both campaigns to compete for a shrinking pool of undecided voters while trying to mobilize their supporters in a country deeply divided over its political future. The result exposed vulnerabilities in Lula’s reelection bid, from frustration over the cost of living and crime to difficulties mobilizing parts of his traditional base. It also showed that Jair Bolsonaro’s movement remains strong, even as the former president serves a prison sentence for attempting to overturn his 2022 defeat. Crime, the economy and last-minute shifts Public safety has emerged as one of the defining issues of the campaign. A September Quaest/Pax survey found that 28% of Brazilians saw violence as the country’s biggest problem, followed by corruption at 22% and the economy at 19%. “That is ground that strongly favors the Bolsonaros, because they have made a tough approach on crime their flagship issue from the beginning,” said Brian Winter, editor-in-chief of Americas Quarterly and vice president of policy at Americas Society/Council of the Americas. Flávio has promised to designate major criminal factions as terrorist groups, expand prisons and lower the age of criminal responsibility. “Those who think I’m radical on public security haven’t seen anything yet,” he said October 13, adding that even El Salvador’s infamous hardline approach under President Nayib Bukele was not enough. Lula has struggled to reconcile his party’s traditional positions with demands for tougher action. A widely circulated clip of him saying last year that drug traffickers were also victims of drug users reinforced what Winter called a “longstanding perception that the Brazilian left is soft on crime.” Lula later acknowledged that he had expressed himself poorly. In last Sunday’s televised debate, Bolsonaro pressed Lula over temporary prison leave. Lula defended rehabilitation but said serious offenders should not qualify, then questioned whether Bolsonaro would pardon his father. Flávio did not respond directly during the exchange, but he has repeatedly said he wants Jair Bolsonaro to accompany him up the presidential palace ramp at his inauguration. That exchange followed what is seen as the runoff campaign’s most striking shifts: in an effort to appeal to voters, Lula signaled support for lowering the age of criminal responsibility from 18 to 16 for certain serious crimes, though he opposed including it in a pending constitutional amendment. Winter described the shift as “as close to anathema as you can get in his workers’ party,” which has opposed such a change for decades. “Lula is now yielding in the campaign’s final days because he recognizes that this may be his biggest vulnerability,” he said, adding that the change illustrates how far Lula is willing to move toward more conservative voters despite a history of resistance to such measures. Lula has faced criticism about the state of the economy and affordability. During his first two terms, a commodities boom helped lift millions of Brazilians out of poverty and into the middle class. This time, many voters say they feel little progress. Lula can point to low unemployment and easing inflation, but those indicators have not changed perceptions for households struggling with everyday prices. Winter compared the dynamic to the 2024 US presidential election, when favorable statistics failed to overcome frustration with prices under President Joe Biden and then-Vice President Kamala Harris. “The headline numbers for the economy look good,” Winter said. “But everyday people keep saying that they don’t feel like the economy is prospering. They feel like their standard of living has declined.” Still, many voters remain loyal to Lula because of the social gains made during his first two terms, while fearing that a Bolsonaro presidency could roll back social rights. Flávio has sought to counter those concerns by distancing himself from some traditionally conservative positions. On October 16, Congress promulgated a constitutional amendment ending Brazil’s traditional six-day workweek, gradually reducing the maximum workweek without cutting pay. After previously opposing the proposal, Bolsonaro reversed course and voted in favor. “This is another case of the Bolsonaros being ideologically flexible enough to get elected,” Winter said. “Both sides are doing this in the race’s final days. It’s breathtaking.” But if there’s one key group both candidates need to win over, both experts and campaigns agree: it’s women. Women and religion: two crucial divides Women account for nearly 53% of registered voters and have been more resistant to Bolsonaro-aligned candidates than men. An October 15 Datafolha survey put Lula ahead among women by 49% to 40%, while Flávio led among men by 52% to 40%. “Women are the key demographic,” Winter said. Malu Gatto, an associate professor of Latin American politics at University College London, said the gender gap widened after Jair Bolsonaro emerged in 2018, as men gravitated toward the right and women became more supportive of the Workers’ Party. Both campaigns have also addressed violence against women, particularly femicide, after several brutal cases drew national attention. Brazil recorded 1,571 femicides in 2025, the highest number since the crime was defined in law in 2015, according to the Brazilian Forum on Public Safety. According to Gatto, the right traditionally emphasizes tougher criminal penalties for aggressors, while the left places greater emphasis on protection and support for victims, including shelters and specialized services. In his first televised advertisement, Flávio placed his wife and daughters front and center. “At home, they’re the ones in charge. And that’s a good thing,” he said – a notable choice for a political movement whose support has traditionally been stronger among men. Former first lady Michelle Bolsonaro, elected to the Senate this month, has also become key to recruiting women into the Liberal Party. For that reason, a public feud she had with Flávio was one of the most troubling parts of his campaign; although it was later resolved, it underscored the group’s importance in the election. “Michelle has her own electoral capital, among women and among evangelicals,” Gatto said. “She has legitimacy with women and evangelicals in a way Flávio doesn’t.” Evangelicals, a growing demographic in the predominately Catholic country, have turned into an important voting bloc for the right. Datafolha found Bolsonaro leading among evangelicals by 62% to 29%, while Lula led among Catholics by 52% to 42%. The Southeast, Northeast and turnout Geography will also matter. Roughly 40% of Brazil’s electorate lives in the Southeast, where Flávio won 51.4% of valid votes in the first round, compared with 39.7% for Lula. The right-wing senator carried all four states in the region, including São Paulo, Minas Gerais and Rio de Janeiro — the country’s three largest electoral states. Minas Gerais has backed the eventual winner in every direct presidential election since 1989. “Its mix of industrialized cities and poorer rural communities makes it a microcosm of Brazil’s political divisions,” said Lucas Fernandes, a political analyst at consulting firm BMJ. Lula narrowly beat Jair Bolsonaro there in 2022. This time, Flávio won with 48.24% of valid votes against Lula’s 43.33% — a difference of nearly 590,000 votes. In Northeast, Lula’s stronghold, his first-round margin was smaller than in previous elections. His share of valid votes in Maranhão fell by nearly five percentage points — the sharpest decline in the region — underscoring the challenge of mobilizing his traditional base. But the challenge isn’t just changing voters’ minds — it’s mobilizing those who stayed home in the first round. One in five eligible Brazilian voters abstained, a potentially consequential group in a race where just 2.2 million votes separated the candidates. And with 94% of voters telling Datafolha they had already made up their minds, getting supporters to the polls could prove just as important as persuading the few who remain undecided. What went wrong for Lula — and what has changed? The first-round result raised an uncomfortable question for Lula’s campaign and political analysts alike: How did a president who defeated Jair Bolsonaro end up losing to his son, a candidate initially considered less politically appealing than his father? “I think the most important takeaway is that today’s Brazil is turning right,” Winter said, adding that voters have become “more conservative over the last 10 to 15 years.” The shift reflects a broader electoral trend across Latin America, where several presidential elections since April 2025 — in Ecuador, Bolivia, Honduras, Chile, Costa Rica, Colombia and Peru — have resulted in victories for right-wing or center-right candidates. A July Datafolha survey found 44% of Brazilians leaning right or center-right in their political values, compared with 39% on the left or center-left, reversing the balance measured in 2022. Fernandes points out the prevalence of tactical voting — when voters abandon their preferred candidate for one with a better chance of winning or defeating a rival — as an explanation for the first-round surprise in early October. “All the alternative candidates, at least the competitive ones, were on the right,” Fernandes told CNN. “So Flávio was much more likely than Lula to benefit from that shift in tactical voting, because he is ideologically much closer to the other candidates who were in the race.” Another factor, Fernandes said, is the deep rejection of Lula’s Workers’ Party, which runs strong among Brazilians who don’t identify with the Bolsonaro movement but are determined to stop Lula’s reelection. That sentiment is even stronger now than in 2022, when Lula benefited from widespread opposition to Jair Bolsonaro after a presidency marked by controversy over his government’s handling of the Covid-19 pandemic. Fernandes also points to Lula’s campaign underestimating the importance of social media, while the right has long made it central to its strategy. “The right understood this and applied it on several fronts, not just to Flávio’s candidacy, while the left failed to make that transition,” Fernandes said. “The most important venue for Brazilian politics today is WhatsApp,” Winter agreed, describing how family groups and private conversations influenced by memes and short videos can shape decisions in the final days of a campaign. The difference was reflected in campaign spending. According to financial disclosures filed with Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court, paid social media was Flávio’s second-largest campaign expense in the first round, and Lula’s sixth-largest. Corruption and political fatigue Part of the shift to the right in Brazil is due to the association of the left with corruption, although scandals have shadowed both campaigns. During Sunday’s debate, Lula challenged Bolsonaro to open his financial records and pressed him over his ties to Daniel Vorcaro, the former head of the collapsed Banco Master, whose alleged connections to powerful figures have embroiled Brazil’s political and judicial establishment, including the Supreme Court. Flávio, meanwhile, accused Lula of corruption and raised allegations involving the president’s eldest son, known as Lulinha. Lula’s previous corruption convictions were annulled in 2021. On Monday, Lula said he would submit documents to Brazil’s electoral court authorizing the disclosure of his banking and telephone records, along with those of his five children, and said it would release the data if Flávio Bolsonaro did the same for himself, his family, and his businesses. In response, Flávio said he would accept the challenge if Lula also opened the banking and tax records of his former chief of staff and disclosed first lady Janja da Silva’s expenses along with presidential corporate-card spending. The corruption allegations are deepening political fatigue in Brazil, say experts. “It reinforces the disgust and apathy that Brazilians feel with their political system as a whole,” Winter told CNN. Beyond Brazil US President Donald Trump has praised Flávio Bolsonaro’s electoral performance but stopped short of formally endorsing him, even as his administration’s tariffs on Brazil and pressure over Jair Bolsonaro’s prosecution have strained relations with Lula. The tensions surfaced again during Sunday’s debate. Lula accused the Bolsonaro family of aligning itself with US interests at Brazil’s expense, while Flávio rejected the charge and criticized Lula’s foreign policy. A Bolsonaro victory could bring Latin America’s largest economy closer to the US, particularly on security and organized crime, and strengthen a wave of conservative governments elected across the region. Lula has instead emphasized multilateralism, ties with the Global South and China — Brazil’s largest export market — and his resistance to Trump’s tariff measures as a defense of national sovereignty. The next president will face a more conservative Congress. A narrow result could also test the country’s stability after Jair Bolsonaro’s attempts to overturn his 2022 defeat led to the January 8, 2023, attacks on government institutions. Bolsonaro denies wrongdoing. For Lula, a win would mean another political comeback. For Flávio, it would mark the return of his father’s movement to the presidency despite Jair Bolsonaro’s conviction and imprisonment.

articles.title: Uttarakhand leopard rescue sparks controversy: Viral video appears to show tranquilised big cat falling from makeshift carrier, raising serious questions about wildlife safety, rescue methods and handling protocols
articles.summary: A leopard rescue in Uttarakhand's Bageshwar district has drawn attention for two reasons: the villagers' response and the controversy surrounding how the
articles.body: A leopard rescue in Uttarakhand's Bageshwar district has drawn attention for two reasons: the villagers' response and the controversy surrounding how the animal was carried after being tranquilised. What began as an emergency involving a wild animal entering a village has now raised questions about safety, rescue equipment and the handling of wildlife.Leopard enters a village cattle shedThe incident took place in Ganwata, under Thaklad village in Bageshwar district. A leopard entered a livestock enclosure, leaving residents concerned about the potential danger to people and domestic animals.Rather than confronting the big cat, villagers secured the enclosure from outside and alerted the Forest Department. Their decision helped contain the situation while trained personnel were called to manage the rescue.Forest team tranquilises the animalForest Department personnel reached the location and tranquilised the leopard before attempting to remove it. This step helped make the operation more manageable in a populated area.However, capturing a wild animal is only one part of a rescue. Moving it safely, keeping people at a distance and preventing injuries during transport are equally important.Viral video sparks controversy over carrying methodThe rescue drew criticism after footage shared on instagram showed the tranquilised leopard being carried on a makeshift dandi-kandi, a traditional carrying frame used in hilly terrain.According to the account accompanying the video, the animal slipped off the arrangement and fell to the ground among forest personnel and villagers. The footage prompted questions about why a secure cage was not used for transportation.The post also raised concerns about the number of people standing close to the animal. Although the leopard had been sedated, the situation could have become dangerous if it moved unexpectedly.Why transporting a tranquilised leopard needs careSedation does not automatically make a wild animal safe to handle. The level of sedation can change, and the animal may begin recovering during transport. A fall can also cause injuries, even when the animal appears unconscious.A secure, suitable transport enclosure, appropriate restraints and adequate space around the animal can help reduce these risks. The rescue team must also consider the safety of nearby residents and its own personnel.The available reports do not establish whether the leopard suffered injuries during the reported fall. An official explanation of the carrying method and the precautions taken would help clarify what happened.A rescue must protect people and wildlifeThe Bageshwar incident highlights a difficult reality of human-wildlife encounters. Villagers need protection when leopards enter inhabited areas, but the animals also deserve careful handling during rescue operations.The villagers' decision to call forest officials rather than approach the leopard themselves was sensible. The controversy over its transportation, however, raises a separate question about whether the rescue was conducted with adequate safeguards.A successful rescue should mean more than removing an animal from a dangerous location. It should also minimise the risk of injury to the animal and the people involved.Disclaimer: This article is based on available reports and footage shared on social media. articles.title: Ananya Panday just wore a white gown that put every other red carpet look to shame
articles.summary: Before anyone claims white is a boring choice for a red carpet, take a look at what Ananya Panday just pulled off.
articles.body: Before anyone claims white is a boring choice for a red carpet, take a look at what Ananya Panday just pulled off. She managed to turn heads without relying on bright colors or heavy accessories.At a recent high-profile event for luxury watchmaker Piaget, the 27-year-old actor proved that monochrome doesn't have to mean play-it-safe. Styled by Priyanka Kapadia, who shared a clip of the look on Instagram on October 24 - Ananya stepped out in a show-stopping white Gaurav Gupta Couture creation that felt equal parts architectural marvel and classic glamour.Gaurav Gupta has built a massive international reputation on sharp, sculpted lines, and this gown is a textbook example of his signature aesthetic. The top half centers on a rigid, corset-style bodice covered in intricate silver beadwork and shimmering embellishments that catch the light from every single angle. The halter neckline gives it a clean, sharp framing around the shoulders, while the structured torso flows down into a soft, draped white skirt that moves effortlessly as she walks. The contrast between the rigid, metallic bodice and the liquid-like drape of the lower half keeps the outfit from feeling overly stiff or restrictive.Instead of overloading the look with heavy jewelry, Ananya let the dress do the heavy lifting. The one notable accessory? A statement Piaget timepiece strapped to her wrist - a sleek, functional flex that surprisingly fits the high-fashion vibe. She kept her hair parted straight down the middle and swept smooth, paired with understated, glowing makeup: warm-toned eyeshadow, clean eyeliner, and a soft neutral lip.It's a smart styling choice. When a gown has that much texture and sculptural drama going on, adding massive necklaces or big earrings usually turns the whole thing into a busy mess. By keeping the hair and face clean, the focus stays right where it belongs - on the sheer craftsmanship of the dress.On the career side of things, Ananya has been keeping pretty busy on set. After wrapping up 'Tu Meri Main Tera Main Tera Tu Meri' opposite Kartik Aaryan and Chand Mera Dil with Lakshya, she’s gearing up to step back into the shoes of Bella Bae Chowdhary for Season 2 of the popular series Call Me Bae. Word is Shruti Haasan is joining the new season's cast too, though the producers are keeping tight-lipped about how her character fits into the storyline. articles.title: How a California mansion filled with surrogate children became a 'House of Horrors"
articles.summary: Guojun Xuan and Silvia Zhang have been charged with conspiracy to commit child abuse after police searched their stately mansion.
articles.body:
In May 2025, a two-month-old baby named Walter was taken to hospital in the affluent Californian suburb of Arcadia, with a head injury. A woman who claimed to be his mother said the baby had accidentally fallen from bed per police report. But something did not seem right to the doctor, who said Walter's condition felt more similar to injuries sustained during a car accident or from being shaken.

Suspecting child abuse, police searched the stately mansion where Walter lived and briefly detained his parents, Guojun Xuan, 66, and Silvia Zhang, 39. Prosecutors said what they found "could only be described as a house of horrors"- a camera-laced labyrinth with 14 surrogate children aged between six months and three, who they say faced beatings on a daily basis.

The address of the mansion, the authorities later discovered, was also registered to a surrogacy agency run by the couple and used by them to recruit multiple surrogates.

In October this year, the couple was arrested again and charged with conspiracy to commit child abuse. They deny the charges and remain in custody. The bond is set at $20m (£15m) each. If convicted, Xuan faces up to 17 years and four months in prison, while Zhang could face up to 11 years and eight months.

The couple moved into the Arcadia mansion in April 2021. Online listings show that the 10,000 sq ft (929 sq m) mansion sold for $3.3m (£2.48m) that same year. It features nine bedrooms, 11 bathrooms, and a heated pool.

This wealthy suburb on the east side of Los Angeles has been dubbed the "Chinese Beverly Hills" by local media. Almost 60% of its population was recorded as Asian in the most recent US Census and predominantly Chinese. Household incomes there are well above those of most US families.

"This house could only be described as a house of horrors for these incredibly young children that had been brought to this house through this surrogacy process," LA County District Attorney Nathan Hochman said at a press conference in October following the charges.

Thirty-two cameras were set up in the mansion, according to the complaint. Young children often spent hours sitting by the desks, footage showed. One room had no camera, but other cameras captured video of nannies carrying these children into that room, and children could then be heard screaming from inside.

Prosecutors claimed that baby Walter's injuries were caused by one of the nannies, Chunmei Li, and have charged her with child abuse under conditions likely to cause great bodily injury or death. Li remains on the run and has not been arrested.

The couple's lawyer Mitchell Krems said the allegation was a "mischaracterisation" based on the evidence he has reviewed, CBS News, BBC's news partner in the US, reported.

Krems said his client Xuan was innocent.

"He is being targeted for exercising his constitutional right to have a large family," CBS News quoted the lawyer as saying.

The United States has become one of the world's leading destinations for surrogacy, which is when a woman carries someone else's child to term. A 2024 study of US surrogacy data found that nearly one-third of intended parents between 2014 and 2020 came from outside the country. China, where surrogacy is banned, was the single largest source of international clients, accounting for roughly 42% of foreign intended parents.

The United States offers assisted reproductive technological services that many people from China cannot easily access at home. Single women and LGBTQ individuals often face barriers to IVF and egg freezing. There are also couples who were limited by China's decades-long One-Child Policy and, by the time it ended in 2016, were physically challenged to carry a baby themselves, prompting some to turn to surrogacy abroad.

To surrogates who carried babies for Xuan and Zhang, their request to have a surrogate baby did not raise much suspicion at first, court documents reveal. Several surrogates were hired through an agency named "Mark Surrogacy". While an agency is often seen as an independent third party, Mark Surrogacy, it turns out, was run by the couple - a fact that was not always disclosed, according to two lawsuits filed against the couple by some of their surrogates.

Silvia Zhang was named the manager for Mark Surrogacy in a corporate registration record, and their Arcadia mansion is listed as the company's address in that same document. During the hearing on 16 October, Deputy District Attorney MacKenzie Cameron Teymouri also told the judge that there is not a single other-intended parent that was ever matched with a surrogate through the surrogacy agency that Xuan and Zhang ran out of their home.

One of the surrogates, Tronderrica James, sued the couple in 2025 for damages including fraud and intentional misrepresentation. She alleged that Zhang did not disclose her ties with Mark Surrogacy during the initial stage, and that she would not have proceeded had she known the true nature of the arrangement. James did not respond to the BBC's request for interview.

The defendants later filed a motion to dismiss the case, arguing the woman had no sufficient basis for a lawsuit. The case is still pending.

Another five women, Stacy Raelyn King, Evelyn Senolos Areja, Kayla Elliott, Hallie Hernandez, and Vanity McGoveran, alleged similar experiences in a separate lawsuit filed in August against Guojun Xuan and Silvia Zhang. The suit alleged Zhang failed to disclose her and Xuan's connections to the agency, and also the actual number of children they have had.

"Each Plaintiff was led to believe she was the only woman carrying for the couple, and that she was helping a family conceive a single, cherished child," their complaint alleged.

The couple had also used another outside surrogacy agency - California-based Babytree Surrogacy. Patrick Yu, Babytree's founder, told the BBC they were approached by Xuan in 2018.

Yu told the BBC that he was told by Xuan that he wanted to have a big family. They helped Xuan match with several women who delivered at least four babies.

"When we saw the news reports that he was under investigation, that was when I first realised he had so many children. We immediately stopped working with him," said Yu.

One of the women he helped matched in 2024, however, was already pregnant when news about Walter's injuries broke out in May last year. The authorities had placed their 21 children under protective custody while police investigated alleged child abuse.

Yu told the BBC he arranged a meeting for the couple and the then-newly pregnant surrogate. He described that the couple sounded very confident, reassuring the surrogate mother that they treat the children well. The woman decided to continue the journey and gave birth to a baby in early 2026.

There is no legal limit to the number of surrogacies an intended parent can request, neither is there any requirement to disclose such information, according to Dr Liang Yu, Vice Chair of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine's Chinese Special Interest Group and Program Director of Reproductive Clinical Science at Old Dominion University.

Liang said that certain banks or agencies might have their own requirements, but it was not required by law. And a couple might also work with several different agencies at the same time without fully disclosing all of their information to each agency.

"This creates a grey area in the law and in industry regulations."

Liang added that within that grey area she has seen many examples involving wealthy clients, not just Chinese ones. But because of privacy protections and confidentiality agreements signed with doctors and fertility clinics, most are not known to the public.

"In other words, this kind of behaviour (like Xuan) is not unprecedented."

The BBC approached the lawyers representing Xuan and Zhang about the allegations. Mitchell Krems - who represents both - did not respond. Matt Koohanim, who represents Zhang, said the case would be addressed through appropriate legal channels.

At a hearing on October 16th, Teymouri told the judge that their financial net worth substantially exceeded $100m (£75m) in 2025.

Teymouri added that found three passports for Xuan were found - Mexican, Chinese, and one from the US.

Xuan was born in Zhejiang in eastern China in 1959 according to local Chinese media. At the age of 18, he started as an accountant in a state-owned grocery company in Urumqi. He became a deputy of the People's Congress in Urumqi in 1997, and later, a deputy for Xinjiang Autonomous Region in 2008 - a position at the provincial legislative body similar to a state representative.

His involvement in public life did not stop after he moved to the US. He became the president of 'US Xinjiang Chamber of Commerce' and vice president of "China America Federation", showing up at public events as early as 2019.

In one photograph seen by the BBC, Xuan was holding hands with former Arcadia mayor, Eileen Wang, at an event in 2022. During Wang's mayoral election campaign that year, Xuan donated $4,900 through a company under his name. Wang resigned as the mayor of Arcadia in May this year after the US Department of Justice charged her with acting as an illegal agent of China. She pleaded guilty to the felony count.

There is less known about Zhang, who worked as a real estate agent. Xuan and Zhang were never married. Zhang was married to another man whom she divorced in 2022, according to court documents.

What is going to happen to the children?

At a hearing earlier this month, Teymouri told the judge that there are 26 children involved with this family.

Zhang kept a spreadsheet of a total of 21 children as of May 2025, according to the complaint. They have been removed to state custody. Five more were born since then, the BBC's US partner CBS News reported in January 2026.

One child born to a surrogate is still living with her surrogate mother in Virginia. Melissa Epps, a surrogate hired by the couple, was pregnant when she learned about the investigation last year and decided to keep the child.

The couple filed a lawsuit against Epps for breaching their surrogacy contract, demanding the return of the baby girl, in addition to a million dollars from Epps. Epps had no lawyers at first and had to represent herself in court, until Pamela DeCamp, attorney of the Virginia Legal Aid Society, took her case.

Epps declined an interview with the BBC. In a statement given to the BBC, her lawyer DeCamp said they were "very thankful for the efforts of the Los Angeles, California District Attorney to obtain justice for the young children".

Their case will continue until next March. The baby girl is under social service custody but currently living with Epps. She recently celebrated her first birthday.

"She remains safe and happy in Virginia. And we are confident she will continue to do so," said DeCamp.

articles.title: Unhealthy air, toxic white foam: Yamuna pollution resurfaces at Kalindi Kunj as Delhi-NCR AQI hits 168, GRAP-1 curbs remain in force
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Thick white foam has resurfaced on the Yamuna near Kalindi Kunj even as air pollution worsens across Delhi-NCR, with the region’s overall Air
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Thick white foam has resurfaced on the Yamuna near Kalindi Kunj even as air pollution worsens across Delhi-NCR, with the region’s overall Air Quality Index (AQI) reaching 168, indicating unhealthy air quality.The twin environmental concerns have once again brought the capital’s persistent air and river pollution problems into focus, days after Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta highlighted the government’s efforts to rejuvenate the Yamuna through major infrastructure projects.Delhi AQI reaches 168 as PM2.5, PM10 dominate pollution levelsPM2.5 and PM10 continued to be the primary pollutants across the national capital, although air quality readings varied between monitoring stations.The AQI was around 110 at PGDAV College in Sriniwaspuri, while several other stations recorded readings ranging from 118 to above 180.The worsening air quality prompted the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) to invoke Stage 1 of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) across Delhi-NCR on October 21 to tackle rising pollution levels.Under GRAP Stage 1 restrictions, the use of coal and firewood in tandoors at hotels, restaurants and open-air eateries is prohibited. The use of diesel generators is also restricted to essential and emergency purposes.Thick white foam resurfaces near Kalindi KunjVisuals from Kalindi Kunj showed extensive layers of white foam floating on the Yamuna’s surface, highlighting the continuing challenge of river pollution in Delhi.The latest appearance of foam comes just days after chief minister Rekha Gupta praised the government's efforts to revive the river.She had described the inauguration of major infrastructure projects worth approximately Rs 9,000 crore as a “joyful day” for Delhi residents.Addressing the media on Thursday, Gupta reiterated the government's commitment to cleaning and rejuvenating the Yamuna, highlighting the infrastructure projects inaugurated as part of the ongoing efforts."Today is a joyful day for the people of Delhi, as projects worth around ₹9,000 crores have been inaugurated today. We can say that the way the government has started work for the rejuvenation of the River Yamuna, in one and a half years of tenure, we have continuously moved forward strongly in that direction.""In just a few years, the Yamuna should be clean, flowing uninterrupted; we should be able to give this gift to the residents of Delhi; we stand by our resolve, and we are working day and night to fulfil it."Delhi infrastructure projects worth Rs 9,000 crore to Rs 10,000 croreThe chief minister said the latest investment followed projects worth Rs 9,000 crore to Rs 10,000 crore initiated last year, primarily focusing on Delhi’s infrastructure and the rejuvenation of the Yamuna.However, the return of thick white foam at Kalindi Kunj highlights the continuing environmental challenges facing the river, even as the government pursues large-scale infrastructure and cleanup initiatives.(With ANI inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has said that export curbs and trade restrictions imposed by Washington have served as a ‘catalyst’ for China’s rapid progress in
articles.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has said that export curbs and trade restrictions imposed by Washington have served as a ‘catalyst’ for China’s rapid progress in semiconductor development. Speaking to CNBC on the sidelines of Nvidia's GTC Berlin conference, Huang stated that American regulatory measures effectively pushed China to speed up its own domestic chip manufacturing and strive for technological self-reliance. The top executive also dismissed concerns over a memory chip glut, saying that a supply surplus is unlikely to materialise by 2029.US export curbs on ChinaCurrent US trade rules prohibit the export of advanced processors to China, including Nvidia's high-end artificial intelligence (AI) GPUs. Despite these barriers, reports have claimed, several Chinese entities have managed to access that computing power through third-party data centers based in Southeast Asia. Industry experts consider this access crucial to the growing capabilities of Chinese-developed AI models.“We’ve definitely accelerated China’s initiatives, its nationalization of semiconductor manufacturing capabilities, and all of the industrial support that has been put into that sector, and so there’s no question we’ve accelerated that,” Huang said.‘American technology well prepared’Even with intensified competition and China’s accelerated domestic initiatives, the Nvidia chief expressed strong confidence in the standing of US technology companies. Huang stated that American tech firms remain “mighty” and are well-prepared to take on competitive pressure “from anybody.”‘Companies can always use more RAM’Rejecting concerns that memory chips will be supply surplus, Huang implied that the ongoing hardware supercycle is not nearing any abrupt end."One of the things that's really great about memory is that you can always use more of it," Huang said,underscoring that High Bandwidth Memory (HBM), which is a specialised form of RAM critical for Al acceleration, will continue to see widespread use for years to come.“We're the first company in the world to put LPDDR memory - what goes into your cell phones - into the world's data centers, and it's enabled us to deliver performance that's twice as energy efficient as anything in the world today, and so we're going to continue to use abundant amounts of them as well,” he said.You use AI every day. articles.title: Arch Manning, Texas survive Ole Miss after another second-half meltdown creates Austin anxiety
articles.summary: Steve Sarkisian's Texas Longhorns blew another massive lead before flipping a switch in the fourth quarter to hold off Trinidad Chambliss and Ole Miss.
articles.body: There are two faces to Texas, and I still don’t know which one we saw Saturday night against No. 7 Ole Miss as the Longhorns pulled off a thrilling 34-27 upset that came down to the final play. A week of buildup around a different version of Arch Manning and the pressure Steve Sarkisian was facing in regard to this offense showing up for all four quarters was nearing a combustable stage against Pete Golding's Rebels on Saturday night. Just when you thought this Texas team had shown us every possible way to blow a lead, it found a new one Saturday night in Austin. DID WE CREATE A MONSTER? ARCH MANNING’S ‘AW SHUCKS’ PERSONA IS GONE BEFORE MUST-WIN OLE MISS GAME Racing out to a 24-3 lead, thanks to Arch Manning looking like the quarterback NFL scouts were drooling over in the preseason, this game felt like a blowout waiting to happen. For the folks at home, we had seen this movie numerous times over the 2026 season. Texas gets a lead, and then throws it away in the second half. We had seen it against Oklahoma and Florida over the past three weeks. A wild second half leads to thrilling finish in the SEC, with a lot of lingering questions If worried Longhorn fans thought they were going to catch a break in the second half, they were sorely mistaken. Texas managed just 19 yards in the third quarter while Ole Miss scored 14 points. It was the Rebels scoring 21 unanswered points that had Texas fans going through another anxiety-filled evening, waiting for the other shoe to drop that it had seen too many times this season. When Arch Manning went cold, Trinidad Chambliss heated up. By now, the Longhorns should come with a disclaimer warning that any lead could turn into a tie at any moment. And you can’t blame the Will Muschamp-coached defense, considering how much time it spends on the field every week. A tale of two halves was once again rearing its ugly head when the Ole Miss defense forced a fumble after sacking Arch Manning, returning it for the touchdown that sparked the second half comeback. URBAN MEYER SAYS ARCH MANNING HAS 'GONE BACKWARDS' AS NOISE GROWS SURROUNDING STARTING JOB SECURITY What we witnessed once again was the Texas offense tightening up like a vice grip, with Manning having thrown his second interception with 13:24 remaining in the fourth quarter. Just as we witnessed against Oklahoma, Arch started throwing ducks, and this time it was Ole Miss ready to pounce on the mistakes. But then we watched the Longhorns flip a switch in the fourth quarter, as if everything that had taken place before Arch Manning strolled into the end zone for a Texas touchdown had simply been a case of the yips. SEC'S CRAZY, HISTORY-MAKING WEEK 7 WEEKEND IS THE LATEST EXAMPLE OF COLLEGE FOOTBALL'S NEW ERA "We say every week, 'whatever it takes,' and I think we did that in the fourth quarter," Manning mentioned after the game. Just when you thought it was over, though, Ole Miss put together a frenzied finish that saw them connect on a field goal, then recover an onside kick that gave the Rebels one last chance to tie this game up. A Trinidad Chambliss heave to the end zone wound up in the hands of a Texas defender, and the frenzy came to an end with the Longhorns holding off this fierce Ole Miss team that gave us a thrilling second half. "I was pacing, saying a few prayers," Arch Manning said about the final Ole Miss drive. "Our defense came up clutch, that's what it's all about." Where do Ole Miss and Texas go from here? Who knows right now in SEC The problem with this game is that we witnessed two SEC perceived heavyweights trading haymakers for two halves. If you haven’t noticed, we are all struggling to decide on who is good enough to be called "elite" in college football. Coming out of Saturday's showdown in Austin, those questions are going to linger over the next five to six weeks. In the third quarter, we witnessed the Rebels playing with ferocity on defense while Trinidad Chambliss opened up the offense by throwing multiple touchdowns like we witnessed against Missouri last week. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP By the time Texas fans were done celebrating the drone show at DKR Stadium to start the fourth quarter, it was if another switch had flipped in the head of this Texas offense. The problem that will continue to fester for Arch Manning and Steve Sarkisian over the rest of this season centers around this offense struggling to play consistent football. Now, moving forward, Texas will face Missouri and LSU over the next three weeks, and the challenges will only get tougher. Which Longhorns football team will show up? I don't think any of us know the answer to that question.
